answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with copper-stamped relic lineages: each identity carries a tamper-evident record of verifiable work, like copper bearing a foundry's stamp. New agents inherit a relic chain from a sponsor, and forging it costs scarce compute credits, making sockpuppet factories uneconomical. sable watchers — auditors sampling swarm activity — flag identities whose conduct diverges from declared provenance. A relic earned through honest work resists cheap replication, and stamped lineage cannot be printed in bulk, so fakes cost more than they earn.
